module_title: Early Medieval Period and Rajputs - Foundation
introduction: The period from 750 AD to 1200 AD is known as the 'Early Medieval Period'. After the death of Harsha, North India fragmented into several smaller Rajput states. This era is characterized by continuous internal struggles for supremacy and the eventual invasions by Turkish conquerors (Ghazni and Ghori).

core_concepts.title: The Tripartite Struggle
core_concepts.description: A prolonged conflict lasting nearly 200 years between three great powers—the Palas (Bengal), the Gurjara-Pratiharas (North-West), and the Rashtrakutas (Deccan)—for the control of the strategic city of 'Kannauj'.

core_concepts.title: Rise of Rajputs and the 'Agnikula' Theory
core_concepts.description: According to Chandbardai's epic 'Prithviraj Raso', Sage Vashistha performed a fire sacrifice (Yajna) at Mount Abu, from which four Rajput clans emerged: Pratiharas, Paramaras, Chalukyas (Solankis), and Chauhans.

core_concepts.title: Invasions of Mahmud Ghazni
core_concepts.description: Mahmud of Ghazni invaded India 17 times between 1000 AD and 1027 AD. His primary motive was to plunder India's wealth. His most famous and destructive raid was on the 'Somnath Temple' in Gujarat in 1025 AD.

core_concepts.title: Muhammad Ghori and Battles of Tarain
core_concepts.description: Unlike Ghazni, Ghori aimed to establish an empire in India. In the First Battle of Tarain (1191), Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Ghori. However, in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), Ghori defeated Prithviraj, laying the foundation of Muslim rule in India.

important_entities.name: Prithviraj Chauhan (III)
important_entities.significance: The most famous Chauhan ruler who ruled over Delhi and Ajmer, known for his fierce resistance against Muhammad Ghori.

important_entities.name: Mahmud Ghazni
important_entities.significance: A Turkic conqueror from Central Asia who treated India solely as a source of immense wealth.

important_entities.name: Jaichand
important_entities.significance: King of Kannauj, who was defeated and killed by Muhammad Ghori in the Battle of Chandawar in 1194 AD.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse their objectives. Remember, Mahmud Ghazni's main objective was only to 'plunder wealth', whereas Muhammad Ghori's objective was to 'establish an empire' in India.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Palas, Pratiharas, and Rashtrakutas fighting for Kannauj.

exam_strategy_tips: The years, participants, and outcomes of the First (1191) and Second (1192) Battles of Tarain are highly frequently asked.
Who was the ruler of Gujarat during Ghazni's attack on Somnath? (Answer: Bhima I) - This is a common objective question.
